key_insight: A differentiable, matrix-free JAX finite-element solver enables GPU-accelerated simulation of large-deformation aortic-valve shells with contact.
engineering_relevance: Faster patient-specific valve simulations could support studies of how tissue properties and geometry affect leaflet deformation and coaptation.
method: Energy-based finite-strain extensible-director shells with hyperelastic materials and finite-range repulsive contact.
Regularized matrix-free Newton–Krylov equilibrium solver with two-level preconditioning.
Automatic differentiation for tangent-vector products and GPU-parallel element and quadrature computations.
evidence_signal: Component benchmarks and contact-free sensitivity checks supported verification; three patient-specific valves reached relative equilibrium residuals below 10^-4, with median GPU runtimes of approximately 15–25 minutes and 5.3–6.5× speedups over corresponding CPU runs.
watch_item: Sensitivity validation was limited to a contact-free plate, so gradient accuracy for valve simulations with evolving contact remains to be established.
paper_title: A Differentiable, GPU-Accelerated Finite-Element Formulation in JAX for Large-Deformation Shells with Contact: Application to Patient-Specific Aortic Valve Simulation
